missing_data: Monthly household spending, emergency-fund floor, healthcare/benefit implications, and any other income disruptions are unknown.
Current coding skill, weekly sustainable study hours, local hiring conditions, and realistic salary floor are unknown.
Lisa's specific conditions for informed agreement and Mark's 12-month success measure are not established.
recommendation: Do not quit or enroll in an immersive bootcamp yet. Keep the job healthy while testing fit and demand through a bounded, part-time experiment: agree with Lisa on protected study/family time and a savings floor; calculate the household budget and benefits exposure; build and deploy one useful automotive-domain project; and seek targeted feedback from software employers or contacts. Set a review date and measurable outcomes (project, sustainable study routine, and credible hiring feedback). Reassess training only if the evidence supports it and the household risk is acceptable. Self-study is not risk-free: its long timeline can stall or cause burnout, so set stop/review rules rather than letting the experiment drift.
strongest_counterargument: Staying employed and studying part-time may defer the earning upside for 18–24 months and add burnout risk; if the current work is the core problem or disciplined study is not sustainable, structured training could improve momentum. Still, the dossier does not establish that an immersive bootcamp or quitting is necessary, and the household runway makes that downside consequential.
